title: Audit trail proxy and retention decisioning API
creator: Alex Kim
description: Build a lightweight audit-trail proxy service that centralizes incoming residency/retention/audit events, evaluates tenant-specific retention decisions via a policy engine, and orchestrates delivery and archival. The proxy acts as a single contract surface for partners to POST evidence and audit records; it performs validation, enrichment (region tags, tenant attributes), idempotency checks, and then routes to: (1) short-term delivery webhook endpoints (customer-provided), (2) long-term archival in the region of record, and (3) an internal immutable ledger for attestation. Key goals: ensure per-tenant residency enforcement, deterministic retention TTL decisions, cryptographically verifiable delivery receipts, and operational visibility for SRE and Compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine evaluates retention/residency flags per-tenant and returns deterministic action (deliver, archive, hold, redact) within 75ms p50
Proxy persists an append-only ledger entry for every accepted event with a signed receipt that can be queried by the Compliance Console
Outbound delivery implements exactly-once semantics for customer webhooks via idempotency keys and at-least-once retry with dead-letter support
Region enforcement: data marked as 'EU-only' must not be routed to non-EU archival or delivery endpoints; automated tests demonstrate enforcement across regions
End-to-end contract tests and one integration test against mock customer endpoints pass in CI with <1% simulated network fault injection failure rate
updates: 2025-01-11: Spike completed — validated policy engine (Open Policy Agent) can express all current residency/retention rules. Performance micro-benchmark attached in design doc.
2025-01-14: Schema v1 agreed with Product & Legal: event envelope includes tenant_id, region_hint, retention_profile, source, client_signature. Added fields for provenance.
2025-01-16: Prototype (PR #7291) implemented basic idempotency and ledger writes to s3-immutable. Added unit tests for idempotency key collisions.
2025-01-18: Code review feedback from SRE — need better backpressure handling and request batching to avoid connection storms. Plan: add token-bucket rate limiter + multiplexed delivery worker pool.
2025-01-20: Integration tests failing under 5k rps synthetic load due to GC pauses in the ledger writer. Investigating switch to append-only journal with background flush.
2025-01-22: Decided to ship initial v0 with single-region support, disabled cross-region replication by default. Follow-up EPIC to add multi-region eventual replication (ENG-63900).
blockers: Need final sign-off from Legal on signed receipt format (RFC-2025-01) — meeting scheduled 2025-01-24
SRE requires SLA for delivery retries; we need to finalize retry budget and backoff policy
risks: High throughput spike could delay ledger flushes leading to longer delivery latency
Policy misconfiguration could cause accidental cross-region leakage if not thoroughly validated
Customer webhook failures could cause backlog growth; must tune dead-letter retention and alerting
implementation_notes: Use OPA for policy evaluation; compile tenant policies into WASM for low-latency evaluation in the proxy
Ledger: append-only JSON lines stored in region-specific immutable buckets; each entry signed with HSM-backed keypair and contains merkle-leaf hash for batch attestation
Delivery: asynchronous workers with at-most-once delivery per idempotency-key; use Redis stream for worker coordination
Operational hooks: tracing headers, per-tenant throttles, feature flag to disable signing for staging clusters
qa_plan: End-to-end tests: contract tests against mock customers, region-enforcement fixtures, chaos injection for network partitions. Manual runbook review with Compliance and SRE before canary.
rollout_plan: Canary in staging -> internal canary for a single pilot customer -> gradual ramp to 10% orgs over 2 weeks -> full enable. Monitor delivery_success_rate and ledger_write_latency during ramp.
notes_for_reviewers: Look closely at the signed receipt schema and the trade-offs for ledger durability vs latency. Suggest focusing review on error semantics for idempotency and how replays are detected.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-64280 (kubernetes operator for HSM key rotation)
